entries.text: Lin selected the microphone. The deck stopped, leaving the thirteen-year-old label beneath its clear cover.
I thought you'd choose the old call. Now that we're recording, all I have is ‘good morning.’
Start with good morning. Don't summarize the station. Say what you know is true right now.
All right. Signal me when the window connects. I won't read from a script.
Zhou raised a hand. Lin leaned toward the microphone, and the red level bars woke with her breath.
“This is Cape Hill Community Radio. Good morning. In our final minute, we can still hear one another.”
When the receive lamp steadied, they climbed the narrow stairs. The first light cleared the antenna.
I wasn't shaking in there, was I? Only now do my fingers feel cold.
Your voice was steady. Ten seconds to the master switch. Watch the lamp; I'll cut the power.
An antenna cable swayed in the wind, carrying its last tremor into the roof beneath their feet.
Did the archive send a receipt? I want to know the words ‘one another’ arrived.
Received: new station call, eight point one seconds complete, marked as the final live record.
Good. It didn't speak for the past. It only left proof that we were here.
Zhou pressed the master switch. The lamp died, and Lin heard wind pass through an antenna no longer transmitting.
